findings.title: Unannotated session parameter in category lookups
findings.problem: The new public functions categories_by_id and require_existing take an unannotated `session` parameter. code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires explicit parameter types in new code and forbids leaving a duck-typed parameter unannotated.
findings.impact: A documented, blocking code-quality standard is violated by a new module; the type is already established in service/hosted_applications/runtime.py (AsyncSession).
findings.recommendation: Annotate `session` as AsyncSession (from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio) in both categories_by_id and require_existing.
findings.check_notes: categories.py now annotates session: AsyncSession in categories_by_id and require_existing and imports AsyncSession from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.

fix.change: Annotated session as AsyncSession in categories_by_id and require_existing

standards_review.notes: All commit subjects in the review range match the documented EPMCDME-####: Description format.
New categories.py functions categories_by_id and require_existing leave the session parameter unannotated; code-quality.md requires explicit parameter types in new code.
Category ids reach SQL only as bound parameters; filter input is size-bounded and validated; no auth bypass or secret logging seen.
